name: Sky Princess
reason: The source title 'Princess Changkong' (changkong = 'vast sky') was rendered literally as 'Sky Princess' to keep the celestial flavor of the imperial title.
description: Royal title of the Crown Prince's younger sister, the emperor's most doted-upon daughter (source: Su Lingyun, Princess Changkong of the Burning Sky Palace). During the succession intrigue she is confined to house arrest alongside the Crown Prince on the orders of the rival princes.

name: Attunement Sanctums
reason: Adaptation term for the sealed cultivation chambers that major sects maintain; it renders the source's generic secret cultivation rooms in a Western fantasy register, with no single source proper noun located.
description: Premium cultivation chambers maintained by powerful sects such as the Skyreach Sect; training inside them is especially beneficial for warriors of the Life-and-Death Realm, and access to them is a coveted privilege.

name: Bronze Forge
reason: The source's 'crafting furnace' of the mad weaponsmith (Xie Lang) was dramatized as the 'Bronze Forge', a mobile mechanical contraption, to fit the adaptation's more visual steam-and-steel register.
description: The massive mobile forge-contraption of the maniacal weaponsmith who abducts Zane from the Lowell estate (Eps 18-20). Zane is carried off inside it until it crashes into a cavern; in the source, Luo Zheng is thrown into Xie Lang's crafting furnace, where he absorbs the Karma Fire Sword.

name: Brandt
reason: The Meng family of Wang Chuan was localized as the 'Brandt family' to give Leo Brandt (source Meng Changjun) a consistent Western family unit.
description: The noble family of Leo Brandt, Zane's ally; known for being shrewd and 'good at reading a room'. The family keeps long-serving retainers such as Jon and considers Zane someone worth cultivating ties with (Eps 72-183).

name: Flynn
issues: Unrelated to the later 'Leroy Flynn' (Eps 1054+); the bare 'Flynn' of Eps 190-192 is a different character and must not be merged with him.
reason: The character's Chinese name Wu Da was fully localized to the Western name 'Flynn', a brisk, athletic-sounding name fitting a driven physical trainee.
description: A talented, obsessively determined outer disciple who made Falcon's Perch (source: Sparrow Hawk Platform) his training ground, scaling the sheer cliff in a thousand-pound weighted suit. He fixates on defeating Zane, the newly minted Adept prodigy, seeing that victory as the only validation that matters (source: Wu Da, who dreams of trampling Luo Zheng).

name: Ralph
reason: An adaptation-named minor servant: the source scene at the Mo residence has only unnamed servants, so the butler was given the Western name 'Ralph' for dialogue clarity.
description: The House Moon butler (Ep 194), condescending toward Ethan's friends until Zane projects a sliver of his Vitality and crushes his spirit, leaving him pale and silent.

name: Wyrmfire
reason: The source sword 'Torch Dragon' (Zhao Zhao's middle-grade spiritual weapon) was renamed 'Wyrmfire', preserving the dragon-and-flame imagery in a Western fantasy register.
description: A prized sword shown off to Zane by its proud owner (Eps 223-224). In the source it is Zhao Zhao's 'Torch Dragon', a middle-grade spirit weapon he uses to cleave Magnetic Auroras on the Sword Radiance Platform.

name: Eastern Reaches
reason: The source geographic term 'Eastern Region' was localized as 'Eastern Reaches' to fit the Western fantasy register of the adaptation.
description: The great eastern territory of the continent where the early story takes place, home to the major sects. Kenneth is its undisputed number-one fighter after Kane's disappearance (Ep 279).

name: Star-Shifting Flag
reason: The source's 'Stars Shifting Banner', Hei Ming's formation flag, was localized as the 'Star-Shifting Flag', a near-literal rendering.
description: Mack's magic array flag, a top-grade Spirit Weapon (Eps 243-244). In the source it is Hei Ming's high-grade spirit tool, prized for the 'Revolving Illusory Array' and runic enchantments engraved on it rather than raw offensive power.

name: Alabaster Peak
reason: The source's 'Jadeite Peak', one of the sect's 33 peaks, was renamed 'Alabaster Peak', swapping one precious-stone name for another better suited to the Western setting.
description: One of the sect's peaks competing in the Peak Competition (Eps 247-248). Nicholas, ranked second among all its disciples, mirrors the source's Yue Qi, the number two of Jadeite Peak, a peak with a deep foundation aiming to reclaim the top of the 33 peaks.

name: Sovereign's Blade
reason: Wang Yanmiao's ancient 'Gentleman Sword', an immortal artifact retrieved from a long-sealed emperor's tomb, was renamed 'The Sovereign's Blade' to preserve its regal provenance for Western listeners.
description: Adrian's (source: Wang Yanmiao's) most cherished weapon, an ancient blade said to have belonged to Emperor Amos of the Draconian Dynasty. He recovered it himself from a trap-filled imperial mausoleum and wields it amid showers of ethereal lotuses in his duel with Zane (Ep 267).

name: Stiletto Hairpins
reason: The paired piercing weapons of Tracy (source: Mo Yuxin, the 'little witch' direct disciple) were named 'Stiletto Hairpins'; the exact source weapon term was not located in the aligned chapters.
description: Tracy's paired short hairpin-daggers, used with her Feather Pricks technique (per the master sheet, from Ep 252 on). She can turn them on her own body to strike sixteen acupuncture points, and keeps them hidden in her palms (Eps 272-284).

name: Vita Shard
reason: The healing pills of Zane's daily allowance in the source were re-imagined as crystalline 'Vita Shards' to match the adaptation's Vitality-based energy system.
description: A basic restorative resource. The Lowell household owes Zane three a day, but the corrupt steward embezzles his allowance down to a single shard (Ep 3; source: Steward Fang skimming Luo Zheng's healing pills).

name: Prince Ray
reason: The Third Prince Su Rui was localized as 'Prince Ray', a short regal name echoing the 'Rui' of his source name.
description: The scheming Third Prince (source: Su Rui), a contender for the imperial succession locked in a wary stalemate with Prince Connor. He hosts the banquet where his young followers challenge Zane, then hands out expensive healing pills with calculated generosity while savoring the entertainment; he never removes a mysterious accessory over one eye, and his spy network tracks Zane's connection to Isla (Eps 341-347).

name: Supreme Aether
reason: The source's 'top-grade True Origin Stone' (worth one million ordinary stones) was localized as the 'Supreme Aether crystal', keeping the one-to-a-million exchange rate against Crystal Cubes.
description: An ultra-dense energy crystal worth a million Crystal Cubes apiece. Two hundred of them power the arched gateway to the trial world, which seals itself once their power is exhausted (Eps 357-358).

name: Finishing Move
reason: An adaptation-coined term formalizing the generic trump-card attacks of the source's Wang family fighters into a named concept, 'Finishing Move'.
description: A single devastating trump-card attack granted to every member of House Warrick, to be unleashed only when the moment is right. The Warrick fighters sent after Zane are eliminated during the Trial checkpoint chaos before they can use theirs (Eps 40-49).

name: Perfect Brushwork
reason: An adaptation-coined name for the flawless rune-inscription technique Zane develops; the source describes his rune-art training under Zong Rui without a matching proper term.
description: The flawless brush technique Zane masters while learning rune arts from the Cloud Hall's rune master (Ep 420 onward); his early attempts are a disaster before his control becomes perfect.

name: Twilight Peak
reason: The source's 'Extreme Yin Mountain', the dangerous site of the Purple Thunder Bamboo, was renamed 'Twilight Peak' to carry the same dark, yin-shadowed connotation in English.
description: A perilous beast-infested mountain where the rare Amethyst Thunderoak (source: five-thousand-year-old Purple Thunder Bamboo) is said to grow; treasure hunters use captured locals as scouts there (Eps 428-430).

name: Soul Shackle
reason: Names the binding that imprisons the Owl Beast's spirit; the source describes it only as chains formed from lightning holding the Moonkin Evil Spirit, with no proper noun, so the adaptation coined 'Soul Shackle'.
description: A lightning-wrought binding etched across the black sphere imprisoning the Owl Beast's spirit (source: the Moonkin Evil Spirit fixed in place by chains of lightning). When Zane breaks it, the soul pressure spikes and arcs of lightning surge into the darkness as the beast gets free (Eps 446-448).

name: Dragon's Heartblood
reason: The source's 'True Dragon Blood', the Fire Dragon Palace's bloodline-enhancing reward, was localized as 'True Dragon's Heartblood' for added gravitas.
description: An immensely precious substance that strengthens a warrior's bloodline, dispensed drop by drop by the Palace as a supreme reward. Madame Vermillion's offer of a single drop to Zane, a boy at the peak of the Adept realm, signals untouchable favor (Eps 449-450; source: Nian Yang's offer of True Dragon Blood from the Fire Dragon Palace).

name: Level Archive
reason: The class-tiered halls of the source's Heavenly Sutra Pavilion (Yellow-class hall and above) were localized as numbered 'Level Archives' (Level 2 Archive, Level 4 Archive, etc.).
description: The tiered technique repositories of the sect's library; most disciples never set foot in the Level 4 Archive, where Zane endures the Purple Shadow's attacks and walks away with the Psyche Spike manual (Eps 51-52; source: the Heavenly Sutra Pavilion and its Xingtian Intent).

name: Chloe
reason: An adaptation-named minor female disciple; no distinct source counterpart is identifiable among the anonymous spectators of the aligned Peak Competition chapters.
description: A young female disciple who watches the Peak Competition bouts alongside Isla from a rooftop, trading banter about the strength of each peak's pledges and fretting anxiously over the brutal fights (Eps 82-85).

name: Starlight Lily
reason: Names the shimmering flower-shaped attacks of Adrian (source: Wang Yanmiao's conjured killing lotuses); the adaptation swapped the lotus imagery for a 'Starlight Lily' and treats it as a resource-infused construct.
description: A shimmering petal construct Adrian conjures and infuses with resources, his third one worth ten thousand points, as a desperation attack against Zane (Ep 91; source: Wang Yanmiao's crushing lotus flowers).

name: Leroy Flynn
issues: Episode pronoun signal reads m0/f1 only because he is always mentioned beside his queen ('her'); both episode dialogue and the source counterpart are male.
reason: The source's Celestial Venerable epithet 'Divine Arrow', the loyal supporter of Queen Xun, was fully localized to the Western name 'Leroy Flynn'.
description: A Supreme Lord unwaveringly loyal to Lavender (source: Xun), one of the three queens of the Demon Night. He watched her dimming King Statue for ages and grabbed his Roaring Token the moment it blazed back to life, defying the Queen of Punishment's demand that he accept a replacement; Lavender once killed a Supreme Lord to help him claim a Crown of Destiny, and he is entering the Five Aging Processes (Eps 1054-1179).

name: No-Fly Ban
reason: Adaptation term for the flight prohibitions that source cities and restricted zones enforce; the source states the rule descriptively without a proper noun.
description: A strict prohibition on flying imposed over certain cities and guarded territories, forcing even powerful cultivators to travel on foot through those zones (Eps 567-1119).

name: Empyrean Realm
reason: The source's 'Empyrean Exalt' tier of supreme experts was localized as the 'Empyrean Realm', folding the title into the adaptation's realm-ladder naming.
description: An exalted cultivation tier of late-story powerhouses; even great clans field only a handful of Empyrean Realm fighters, and they rarely take action in ordinary wars (Eps 456-1165; source: the rare Empyrean Exalts of the Demon Night Clan).

name: Cannibal Moth
reason: The source creatures called 'Black Eating Moths' were renamed 'Cannibal Moths', emphasizing their devouring nature for the Western fantasy register.
description: Swarming devouring moths encountered in the Yin-world tunnels of the late story (Eps 1135-1139; source: the Black Eating Moths of the Sifting Yin World arc).

name: Gideon
reason: The source's mysterious 'Primordial Heavenly Venerate', an ancient being suspected to predate the current universe, was given the personal name 'Gideon' for the adaptation.
description: A long-dead Supreme Lord apparently from the last Cosmic Age, into whose hidden home Zane and Livingston intrude (Eps 1163-1164). The relics he left behind, including a power Gideon himself had used, hint that his origin lies outside the current universe (source: the Primordial Heavenly Venerate whose origin even Xun suspects).

name: Cassian Maren Taryn and Paige
reason: Not an entity: a punctuation-stripped list of four separate character names ('Cassian, Maren, Taryn and Paige') run together by extraction; each name should be tracked individually if needed.

name: Punishment of Eternal Night
reason: The source's 'Eternal Night Punishment' of the Yao Night Clan was localized near-literally as the 'Punishment of Eternal Night'.
description: One of the cruelest punishments of the Night clans: the victim's soul is extracted and locked in the Soul Torture Prison, where there is neither life nor death, only eternal torment. Normally reserved for the clan's most heinous traitors, its mere mention darkens the faces of seasoned warriors (Eps 1170-1318).

name: Northern Sky Region
reason: The source term 'Northern Sky Region' (also rendered 'Northern Heaven Region') was carried over unchanged, already fitting the adaptation's register.
description: A deep-space region of the universe toward which fugitives and the drifting Crown of Heaven's Will flee during the late-story pursuit of Lavender (Eps 1175-1202).

name: Tiger-Taming Sentinel
reason: The Buddhist 'Tiger-subduing Arhats' of the source were renamed 'Tiger-Taming Sentinels', stripping the explicitly Buddhist arhat term for the Western fantasy setting.
description: Four guardian constructs in the Illusion Battlefield trial whose palm strikes release phantom images of ferocious tigers; they withstand Zane's wind blades and arcing lightning until he closes in and breaks them one by one (Eps 1219-1220).

name: Sea of Vitality
reason: The source's 'True Essence Sea' within a cultivator's Inner World was localized as the 'Sea of Vitality', aligning with the show's canonical 'Vitality' energy term.
description: The inner sea of energy that forms within a cultivator's Inner World at the Soul Sea Realm, the cradle from which a world's first low-level life can arise. Zane is exceptional in having a Chaos Sea instead of one, while Sloane's Inner World holds a Sea of Vitality unlike any other cultivator's (Eps 900-1236).

name: Harley
reason: The source character rendered as 'Spark' was localized to the Western name 'Harley'; his death scene is adapted line-for-line (the protective orange light being corroded away).
description: A member of the group racing through the parasite-infested tunnels of the Withered Tree branch run. The orange shield of light protecting him is corroded to nothing and he perishes screaming, spurring the rest of the party to keep moving (Eps 1246-1247).

name: Moonburst Flamebow
reason: The source weapon 'Moon-Shattering Bursting Flame Bow' was compressed into the punchier 'Moonburst Flamebow' for audio delivery.
description: Hailey's signature bow (source: the Moon-Shattering Bursting Flame Bow of a Yao Night Clan woman). Drawing on her own reserves, she conjures a boiling flame vortex before the bow as its devastating shot, and Zane later uses one of its fiery blasts as cover (Eps 1271-1281).

name: Semi-Divine Weapon
reason: The source tier term 'Semi-Divine Tool' (also 'Semi-Divine Artifact') was localized as 'Semi-Divine Weapon', consistent with the show's weapon-tier naming.
description: A weapon grade just below true Divine Arms, treasures held by royalty of the Divine Kingdoms. Fiona's bracelet (source: Huo Yuner's Heavenly Jade Bracelet) is one, as is Fredrick's Heavenly Thunder Halberd (Eps 814-1311).
